title: Talking about past experiences / Kɛlɛya kɛlɛw bɛɛw bɛ mɔgɔkɔrɔfilasira
bridge: Espagnol kan, kɛlɛw bɛɛw bɛ mɔgɔkɔrɔfilasira kɛlɛya, pretérito perfecto compuesto ('he visitado') wala pretérito indefinido ('visité') kan b'a fɔlɔ, a bɛ fɔɔ a tun bɛ yɛrɛ cɛnhɛnkɛyɔrɔ wala a tɛ. Anglikan, kɛlɛw bɛɛw bɛ mɔgɔkɔrɔfilasira kɛlɛya, 'present perfect' ('have visited') b'a fɔlɔ, an ka sɔrɔ sɛbɛn kanu Espagnol kan. Kɔrɔsi tɛ anglikan 'have + participio' b'a fɔlɔ a bɛ sɔrɔ kɛlɛw bɛɛw bɛ yɛrɛ cɛnhɛnkɛyɔrɔ tɛ, hala Espagnol kan pretérito indefinido b'a fɔlɔ a bɛ sɔrɔ kɛlɛw bɛɛw bɛ yɛrɛ cɛnhɛnkɛyɔrɔ tun bɛ. Talenw: anglikan 'present perfect' tɛ a fɔlɔ a bɛ sɔrɔ kɛlɛw bɛɛw bɛ yɛrɛ cɛnhɛnkɛyɔrɔ tun bɛ, 'yesterday' wala 'last year' bɛɛw la.
rule: Anglikan kɛlɛw bɛɛw bɛ mɔgɔkɔrɔfilasira kɛlɛya, 'present perfect' b'a fɔlɔ a bɛ sɔrɔ: have/has + participio pasado. A bɛ fɔlɔ: 1) kɛlɛw bɛɛw bɛ mɔgɔkɔrɔfilasira, yɛrɛ cɛnhɛnkɛyɔrɔ tɛ (I have visited Paris), 2) kɛlɛw bɛɛw bɛ tun bɛ yɛrɛ cɛnhɛnkɛyɔrɔ, nka tɔgɔ bɛ yɛrɛ cɛnhɛnkɛyɔrɔ (She has lost her keys), 3) 'ever', 'never', 'already', 'yet', 'just', 'before' bɛɛw la. A bɛ sɔrɔ 'have not' (haven't) wala 'has not' (hasn't) bɛɛw la fɔlɔ fana. A bɛ sɔrɔ kɛlɛya kɛlɛw bɛɛw bɛ mɔgɔkɔrɔfilasira, 'Have you ever + participio?' b'a fɔlɔ a bɛ sɔrɔ, 'Yes, I have' wala 'No, I never have' bɛɛw la fɔlɔ fana. 'Present perfect' tɛ a fɔlɔ a bɛ sɔrɔ kɛlɛw bɛɛw bɛ yɛrɛ cɛnhɛnkɛyɔrɔ tun bɛ (yesterday, last week, in 2010). A bɛ sɔrɔ 'past simple' (visited, went) bɛɛw la fɔlɔ fana. A2 kan, a bɛ fɔlɔ a bɛ sɔrɔ participios bɛɛw bɛ mɔgɔkɔrɔfilasira (go-gone, eat-eaten, see-seen, have-had).

Kɛlɛw bɛɛw bɛ yɛrɛ cɛnhɛnkɛyɔrɔ tun bɛ, 'past simple' (visited) b'a fɔlɔ a bɛ sɔrɔ. Talenw: 'present perfect' + yɛrɛ cɛnhɛnkɛyɔrɔ tun bɛ = sɔrɔkɛ.

title: Making Plans and Arrangements / Kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu
bridge: Espagnol la, mɛn wɛrɛ fana wala kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu ye a bena a kan kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu. Anglɛ kan, kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu ye a bena a kan kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu, 'present continuous' (I'm meeting) ye a bena a kan kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu, 'be going to' (I'm going to visit) ye a bena a kan kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu. Talaki: Anglɛ kan, mɛn wɛrɛ fana si bena a kan kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu, Espagnol la, mɛn wɛrɛ fana bena a kan kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu (ye. 'Te llamo mañana' → 'I'll call you tomorrow', 'I call you' si). Kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu, 'will' ye a bena a kan kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu.
rule:
Anglɛ kan kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu A2 tɔgɔ la, kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu ye a bena a kan kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu:

1. **Present continuous** (am/is/are + -ing): kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu ye a bena a kan kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu, tɛmɛ kanu ye a bena a kanu. Ye. 'I'm seeing the doctor at 3.' (Kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu ye a bena a kanu).

2. **Be going to** (am/is/are going to + infinitivo): kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu ye a bena a kan kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu, tɛmɛ kanu si bena a kanu. Ye. 'We're going to visit our grandparents.' (Kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu ye a bena a kanu).

3. **Will** (will + verbo base): kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu ye a bena a kan kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu, kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu ye a bena a kan kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu. Ye. 'I'll help you with that.' (Kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu ye a bena a kanu).

4. **Would like to** (would like to + infinitivo): kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu ye a bena a kan kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu. Ye. 'Would you like to come to my party?'

Anglɛ kan, mɛn wɛrɛ fana si bena a kan kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu (Espagnol la, mɛn wɛrɛ fana bena a kan kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu). 'Be going to' wala 'present continuous' ye a bena a kan kɛlɛya kɔgɔ cɛnɛma kanu.

title: Giving advice and recommendations / Kɔjiriw kɛ fɛɛw kanbɛlenw
bridge: Espaɲɛ kan, kɔjiriw kɛ fɛɛw kanbɛlenw don kɛra subjuntiɲɛ (te recomiendo que vayas, deberías ir). Aŋkaloŋo kan, subjuntiɲɛ mana bɛ ka kɛra 'recommend' wala 'suggest' jɔ; mɔgɔkɔrɔsi bɛ se ka kɛra verbi kɛyɔgɔ wala jɛn-kɔrɔsi + infinitif: 'I recommend you go', 'I suggest you try'. Mɔgɔkɔrɔsi bɛ se ka kɛra 'should' (deberías) mɛn ka bɛɛ kɛra 'must' jɔ, tɛmɛna 'should' bɛɛ ka kanbɛlɛn jɛn ka kɛ. Kɔjiriw kɛ fɛɛw kanbɛlenw Espaɲɛ kan don kɛra subjuntiɲɛ: 'I recommend that you go' bɛɛ fana, 'I recommend you to go' mana bɛ ka kɛra Aŋkaloŋo kan, tɛmɛna 'recommend' mana bɛ ka kɛra infinitif 'to' jɔ kɛ jɛn-kɔrɔsi bɛ yɔrɔ.
rule:
Kɔjiriw kɛ fɛɛw kanbɛlenw kɛra Aŋkaloŋo kan A2 tɔgɔ jɔ, kɛra kɔrɔsiw yaaw kɔrɔsiw bɛɛ:
1. **Should / Shouldn't + verbi kɛyɔgɔ**: kɔjiriw kɛ fɛɛw kanbɛlenw kɔrɔw. Ɛndɛ: 'You should eat more vegetables.' 'You shouldn't stay up late.' (kɛlɛmɛ). Mana bɛ ka kɛra kɛlɛmɛ (he should, no he shoulds).
2. **You could + verbi kɛyɔgɔ**: kɔjiriw kɛ fɛɛw kanbɛlenw kɔrɔw wala tɛmɛtɛmɛw. Ɛndɛ: 'You could try yoga.'
3. **I recommend / I suggest + that + jɛn-kɔrɔsi + verbi kɛyɔgɔ** (mana 'to' jɔ wala subjuntiɲɛ kɛlɛmɛ). Ɛndɛ: 'I recommend that you see a doctor.' Mɔgɔkɔrɔsi bɛ se ka kɛra gerundif: 'I recommend seeing a doctor.' wala 'I suggest trying this.'
4. **How about + gerundif (-ing)?**: kɔjiriw kɛ fɛɛw kanbɛlenw kɔrɔw kɛlɛmɛ. Ɛndɛ: 'How about going for a walk?'
5. **Why don't you + verbi kɛyɔgɔ?**: kɔjiriw kɛ fɛɛw kanbɛlenw kɔrɔw kɛlɛmɛ. Ɛndɛ: 'Why don't you take a break?'
Fɛɛw kanbɛlɛn: mana kɛra 'must' kɔjiriw kɛ fɛɛw kanbɛlenw jɔ, tɛmɛna 'must' bɛɛ ka kɛra tɛmɛ jɔ. Kɔjiriw kɛ fɛɛw kanbɛlenw kɔrɔw, kɛra 'could' wala 'might'. Fɛɛw kanbɛlɛn: 'recommend' kɛ 'suggest' jɔ, mana kɛra 'to' jɔ kɛ jɛn-kɔrɔsi bɛ yɔrɔ: 'I recommend you to go' mana bɛ ka kɛra.

common_error.explanation: Espaɲɛ kan, mɔgɔ bɛ se ka kɛra 'te recomiendo que vayas' wala 'te recomiendo ir', amma Aŋkaloŋo kan, 'recommend' jɔ, mana kɛra infinitif 'to' jɔ kɛ jɛn-kɔrɔsi bɛ yɔrɔ. Kɔrɔsi kɛyɔgɔ bɛ se ka kɛra 'recommend + that + jɛn-kɔrɔsi + verbi kɛyɔgɔ' wala 'recommend + gerundif'. Kɔjiriw kɛ fɛɛw kanbɛlenw wɔrɔ bɛɛ kɛlɛmɛ tɛmɛna mɔgɔw bɛ se ka kɛra 'te recomiendo a ti ir' (mɛn ka bɛɛ kɛra 'recommend you to go'). Kɔjiriw kɛ fɛɛw kanbɛlenw wɔrɔ kɛlɛmɛ kɛlɛw, fɛɛw kanbɛlɛn: 'recommend' bɛ se ka kɛra 'that' wala '-ing', mana 'to' jɔ.

title: Expressing opinions / Aɲi jàgaké la (Ayé, An síisii)
bridge: Espagnol kan, i sira ka 'creo que' la 'pienso que' jamana fanga ka kɛra kɛra fanga sira bɛɛ. Nka, angale kan, u fana ka 'I think' yé u fana ka 'I believe' sira tun bɛɛ se ka tugu ka taa u ka jàgaké la u ka sira kelen kɛ kɛ. Kala u tɛ ka 'Yo pienso que' la 'I think that' jamana fanga ka kɛra kɛra fanga sira bɛɛ se. Nka, angale kan, 'that' jamana bɛɛ se ka tugu ka taa u ka jàgaké la u ka sira kelen kɛ kɛ. U bɛɛ se ka tugu ka taa u ka jàgaké la u ka sira kelen kɛ kɛ, u ka jàgaké la u ka sira kelen kɛ kɛ, u ka jàgaké la u ka sira kelen kɛ kɛ. U bɛɛ se ka tugu ka taa u ka jàgaké la u ka sira kelen kɛ kɛ, u ka jàgaké la u ka sira kelen kɛ kɛ, u ka jàgaké la u ka sira kelen kɛ kɛ.
rule:
Aɲi jàgaké la angale kan A2 tugu kɛra:
- 'I think (that) + tugu' – jàgaké la sira kelen kɛ kɛ.
- 'I believe (that) + tugu' – sira kelen kɛ kɛ la jàgaké.
- 'In my opinion, + tugu' – kaɲakan, nka ka kɛra kɛra fanga sira bɛɛ se ka tugu ka taa u ka jàgaké la u ka sira kelen kɛ kɛ.
Kalan fanga bɛɛ se: 'I guess' (ayé) la 'I suppose' (ayé), kalan fanga bɛɛ se.
Fili: 'that' jamana bɛɛ se ka tugu ka taa u ka jàgaké la u ka sira kelen kɛ kɛ. Tugu kɛra: sira kelen kɛ kɛ + tugu. 'Of' la 'on' jamana bɛɛ se ka tugu ka taa u ka jàgaké la u ka sira kelen kɛ kɛ. 'I think in that' jamana bɛɛ se, nka 'I think that' la 'I think' jamana bɛɛ se. Tugu: 'I think (that) it's a good idea', 'I believe (that) he is right'. Aɲi jàgaké la, u ka 'do you think?' jamana bɛɛ se ka tugu ka taa u ka jàgaké la u ka sira kelen kɛ kɛ: 'It's a good idea, do you think?'

title: Agreeing and Disagreeing / Sanakɛla dɔn ka jamana
bridge: Espańe kan, sanakɛla dɔn ka jamana don kɛra 'estoy de acuerdo' ka jamana dɔn, nka, ka tugu jamana don 'no estoy de acuerdo' ka jamana dɔn. Anw fɔlɔ, i kɛra kɔrɔtan dɔkɔrɔtan jamana wɛrɛwɛrɛwɛrɛ fana 'I agree' ka jamana dɔn, 'I disagree' ka jamana dɔn. I tun kɛra 'so do I' ka jamana dɔn, 'neither do I' ka jamana dɔn mɔgɔkɔrɔtɔyɛlɛ fana kɛlɛ ka sanakɛla dɔn ka jamana dɔn, nka, Espańe kan sira b'a fana kɛlɛ. K'a bɛɛ, 'agree' bɛɛ verbɛ ka jamana dɔn, a bɛɛ adjectifɛnni, manti 'I am agree' ka jamana dɔn, nka 'I agree' ka jamana dɔn.
rule: Sanakɛla dɔn ka jamana dɔn fɔlɔ, i kɛra 'I agree' (estoy de acuerdo) ka jamana dɔn, 'I think so' (creo que sí) ka jamana dɔn. Tugu jamana dɔn fɔlɔ, 'I disagree' (no estoy de acuerdo) ka jamana dɔn, 'I don't think so' (creo que no) ka jamana dɔn. Sanakɛla dɔn ka jamana dɔn fɔlɔ, i kɛra 'So do I' (yo también) ka jamana dɔn, 'Me too' (yo también) ka jamana dɔn. Tugu jamana dɔn fɔlɔ, i kɛra 'Neither do I' (yo tampoco) ka jamana dɔn, 'Me neither' (yo tampoco) ka jamana dɔn. I tun kɛra 'Exactly' (exacto) ka jamana dɔn, 'That's right' (es cierto) ka jamana dɔn sanakɛla dɔn ka jamana dɔn fana kɛlɛ. Tugu jamana dɔn fana kɛlɛ fɔlɔ, i kɛra 'I'm not sure' (no estoy seguro) ka jamana dɔn. K'a bɛɛ, 'agree' bɛɛ verbɛ ka jamana dɔn: I agree, you agree, he/she agrees. Sanakɛla dɔn ka jamana dɔn fɔlɔ, i kɛra 'Do you agree?' (¿estás de acuerdo?) ka jamana dɔn.

Anw fɔlɔ, 'agree' bɛɛ verbɛ ka jamana dɔn, a bɛɛ adjectifɛnni, manti a tun b'a taara 'to be' ka jamana dɔn. K'a bɛɛ, 'agree' bɛɛ verbɛ ka jamana dɔn, manti a bɛɛ adjectifɛnni. K'a bɛɛ, i kɛra 'I agree' ka jamana dɔn, 'I don't agree' ka jamana dɔn fana kɛlɛ.

title: Describing Daily Routines / Rutinu jɔlenw kanbɔghɔ
bridge: Espagnol kan, o fɔlɔ filimuw dɔgɔbaw ya-ni o tɛ sɔrɔ minw o flɛ ka ‘yo me levanto’ wala ‘me levanto’ ka refleksi dɔgɔbaw bɛn. Anglɛ kan, o si tɛ refleksi dɔgɔbaw bɛ minw o bɛna rutinu ka fɔlɔ: o tɛ sɔrɔ minw o flɛ ka ‘I get up’. Kɔfɛ, espagnol kan, o bɛɛ minw o tɛ sɔrɔw sɔrɔmɔn o tɛ bɛn (desayuno), nka, anglɛ kan, o bɛn o sɔrɔmɔn ka ‘I’ bɛn (’I have breakfast’). Kɔrɔni fɛ, anglɛ kan, minw o bɛna dɔgɔbaw minw o bɛnna o sara kelen, o bɛnna presɛn simpl ka -s ka jamana nuninw kan (’he gets up’), nka frekwɛnsi adivɛrbi (’always’, ‘usually’) o bɛn o dɔgɔbaww kan, o si tɛ o jamana fɛn ka espagnol kan (’siempre me levanto’ vs. ‘I always get up’).
rule: Anglɛ kan, rutinu jɔlenw kanbɔghɔ fɔlɔ o bɛnna presɛn simpl (present simple). A ka jɛnminw: Sɔrɔ + dɔgɔbaw (ka -s minw o bɛna he/she/it se bɛn) + komplɛmɛn. Frekwɛnsi adivɛrbi (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) o bɛn o dɔgɔbaw din ka bɔ, nka ‘to be’ dɔgɔbaw ka bɔ. Tɛmɛ ka jɔlenw ‘in the morning’, ‘at night’ o bɛn jɔlenw ka taa wala jɔlenw ka jamana. Fila o tɛ sɔrɔmɔn o tɛ bɛn anglɛ kan. Tilaten: ‘I wake up at seven.’ / ‘She always drinks coffee.’ / ‘They go to work by bus.’

title: Talking about health and symptoms / Ka jògòdògòw bɛɛw kanu
bridge: Espagnol kan, mɛn waati min b'a 'tener' ka fɔlɔ fɔ a ka jògòdògòw kanu: 'tengo dolor de cabeza', 'tengo fiebre'. Anglɛ kan, fɔlɔw ye tiɲɛn ye: mɛn b'a 'have' ('I have a headache') jògòdògòw kanu ye, 'feel' mɛn b'a fɔlɔ fɔ a ka jògòdògòw kanu ('I feel sick'). A ka taa ni ye ko mɛn na fɔ 'I have cold' a ye ko 'I have a cold', jiriw la anglɛ kan jògòdògòw kanu 'cold' wala 'headache' bɛɛ min b'an ka fɔlɔw ka kɛlɛ 'a' ye.
rule: Anglɛ kan A2 tɔgɔ la, jògòdògòw kanu bɛɛw ka tɔɔw kanu bɛɛ, waati min b'a fɔlɔw wɔsɔ: 1. **Have + jògòdògòw:** 'Have' bɔra 'tener' ka fɔlɔ fɔ jògòdògòw kanu 'I have a cold' (mɛn ka jògòdògòw ye), 'I have a headache' (mɛn ka jògòdògòw ye), 'I have a toothache' (mɛn ka jògòdògòw ye). Fɔlɔw 'a' bɔra a ka fɔlɔw kanu bɛɛ. 2. **Feel + tɔgɔ:** Jògòdògòw kanu bɛɛw ka tɔɔw kanu bɛɛ, 'feel' + tɔgɔ bɔra: 'I feel tired' (mɛn ka jògòdògòw ye), 'I feel sick' (mɛn ka jògòdògòw ye), 'I feel dizzy' (mɛn ka jògòdògòw ye). 3. **Jògòdògòw kanu:** Jògòdògòw kanu bɛɛw ka tɔɔw kanu bɛɛ, 'I have pain in my back' (mɛn ka jògòdògòw ye) wala 'my back hurts' (mɛn ka jògòdògòw ye). 4. **Verbo 'hurt':** 'Hurt' bɔra jògòdògòw kanu: 'My head hurts' (mɛn ka jògòdògòw ye), 'My stomach hurts' (mɛn ka jògòdògòw ye). 5. **Jògòdògòw kanu bɛɛw ka tɔɔw kanu bɛɛ:** 'What's wrong?' (I jògòdògòw ye?), 'Are you okay?' (I jògòdògòw ye?), 'How do you feel?' (I jògòdògòw ye?). 6. **Jògòdògòw kanu bɛɛw ka tɔɔw kanu bɛɛ:** 'You should see a doctor' (I jògòdògòw ye), 'You shouldn't eat that' (I jògòdògòw ye).

title: Making requests and offers / Kɛlɛya k’a fana a bɔra don
bridge: Espagnol kan, an b’a y’a sɔrɔ kɛlɛya k’a fana a bɔra don, an ka kɛlɛ ni imperativo wala ‘¿Puedes...?’. Anglais kan, an b’a y’a sɔrɔ ‘Can’ ni ‘Could’ ye ni furu jɔlen kan. K’a bɔra don kɛlɛ, espagnol kan, an b’a y’a sɔrɔ ‘¿Quieres que...?’, nka, anglais kan, an b’a y’a sɔrɔ ‘Can I...?’ wala ‘Do you want me to...?’. Talaki: anglais kan, ‘Could you...?’ bena jɔlen kan furu ‘Can you...?’ ye. O b’a ta ye imperativo sanakɛ o bena jɔlen kan furu.
rule:
Anglais kan, A2 tɔgɔ kɔ, kɛlɛya k’a fana a bɔra don, an b’a y’a sɔrɔ: 
- 'Can you + verbo...?' (jɔlen kan, saba ja) 
- 'Could you + verbo...?' (jɔlen kan furu, furu jɔlen kan) 
- 'Would you mind + gerundio?' (jɔlen kan furu, nka o bena mɔgɔkɔrɔfilenye). 
K’a bɔra don kɛlɛ: 
- 'Can I + verbo...?' (A ban b’a...?) 
- 'Do you want me to + verbo...?' (I b’a fana n’a...?) 
- 'Would you like me to + verbo...?' (jɔlen kan furu). 
Talaki: anglais kan, ‘Can’ wala ‘Could’ cɔ, an b’a ta ye ‘to’ verbeyɛrɛyɛn kan ye. K’a bɔra don kɛlɛ, ‘me to’ b’a y’a sɔrɔ ‘want’ wala ‘like’ cɔ.

title: Expressing Ability and Possibility / A ban ye a ka taa sira kanu
bridge: A ban ye a ka taa sira kanu, a taali gianin, 'poder' ye mɔgɔkɔrɔninw loile b'a 'saber' a ye mɔgɔkɔrɔninw loile b'a to jati. A taali gianin, k'a yira ko 'can' (jigiya) ye 'could' (kɔfɛ) bɛna mɔgɔkɔrɔninw loile b'a to jati, amma ma sira kelen kɛ: 'could' a taa lo kelen kɔfɛ la ka taa sira kanu (n'a ta ye ko 'Could you swim?') ye 'be able to' a ta lo jigiya la ka taa sira kanu. A taali gianin, a ka taa sira kanu, 'can' ye 'could' a ta lo sira kanu jigiya, 'may' ye 'might' a ta lo sira kanu ka taa sira kanu ka taa sira kanu, n'a yira ko a taali gianin a ta lo sira kanu ka taa sira kanu.
rule: A ka taa sira kanu jigiya, lo 'can' + gianinw (n'a ta ye ko 'I can swim'). A ka taa sira kanu kɔfɛ, lo 'could' + gianinw (n'a ta ye ko 'I could swim when I was young'). A ka taa sira kanu kɔfɛ la ka taa sira kanu (a ka taa sira kanu), lo 'was/were able to' (ma 'could'). A ka taa sira kanu, 'can' a ta lo sira kanu jigiya (n'a ta ye ko 'It can rain'), 'could' a ta lo sira kanu kɔfɛ (n'a ta ye ko 'It could rain later'), 'may' ye 'might' a ta lo sira kanu ka taa sira kanu (n'a ta ye ko 'She may come'). 'can' ka taa sira kanu ye 'cannot' wala 'can't', 'could' ka taa sira kanu ye 'couldn't'. Ma lo 'to' 'can' wala 'could' ka bana.

title: Talking about weather / Faran ka jamana
bridge: Espagnol la, I ka ne 'faran ka jamana ye' an ka 'faran ka jamana bena' kanu, 'faran' an ka 'ye' jamana koo don. Angale la, I ka ne 'it' jamana koo don 'It is hot', 'It is raining' kanu. K'a kelen ye ko angale la, jamana koo don, I ka ne 'it' jamana koo don, amma espagnol la, jamana koo don sira bena. Faran mɔgɔ minw ka 'weather' angale jamana koo don, o kɔrɔtɔgɛ, I ka ne 'a weather' an ka 'weathers' sira bena.
rule:
Angale A2 la, faran ka jamana kanu, k'a jigi k'a kanw:
1. 'It is' + jɛnɛgɛ: It is sunny, It is cloudy, It is windy, It is cold, It is warm.
2. 'It is' + n'gɛlɛyɛ: It is raining, It is snowing, It is hailing.
3. 'There is' + sɛbɛn: There is a storm, There is fog, There is a rainbow.
4. 'There are' + sɛbɛnw: There are clouds, There are showers.

K'a fɔgɛn an ka k'a sɛgɛsɛgɛ: 'It is hot' an ka 'It is cold' bɛɛ kanu, amma 'It's warm' an ka 'It's cool' bɛɛ kanu. K'a fɔgɛn, I ka ne 'What's the weather like?' an ka 'How's the weather?' (sira b'an ka 'How is the weather?'). K'a taa, 'weather' jamana koo don sira bena: o taa kelen I ka ne 'a weather'.
